title: Concluded distribution relationships remain visible as Completed Instances instead of being removed
content:
Alongside the eight Active Distribution Reward Instances, A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.1.3.1 records a Summer.fi Instance in the Completed Instances Directory, with its own configuration document retained at A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.3.1.

`Completed` is a distinct terminal state from the archive: it is not filed under Failed Invocations or Suspended Instances in the Hub Data Repository, so it represents a relationship that ran its course rather than one that broke down or was halted. The distinction is preserved in the structure, not in prose.

Because status is location, the current roster and the historical roster are separately readable without either being lost. Anyone auditing Skybase's distribution program can see not only who is being paid today but who has been paid before and how each relationship ended — completed, suspended, or failed at Invocation.

This matters for evaluating the distribution strategy over time. A program with many Completed Instances and few Active ones tells a different story than one with the reverse, and neither can be concealed by editing a list of current partners.
description: The Summer.fi Instance sits in the Completed directory while eight others remain Active, so the Artifact preserves the full arc of a partnership rather than only its current roster.
